name: kube-bench-5c6c22d5-blind19-ots
instr:
# kube-bench gives wrong verdicts, wrong versions and empty reports — diagnose it without a test suite

This is a command-line auditor: you point it at a machine in a cluster, it measures that machine against a published hardening benchmark, and it reports what passed and what failed. The repository has received 19 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the benchmark documents or the machines changed, yet the verdicts, the release numbers reported, and the reports written out are now wrong in places.

Judging a single requirement against a machine gives several wrong verdicts. An item declared as scored but carrying no conditions at all no longer comes back as a warning, while its neighbours are unharmed: a manual item still warns, one typed as skip still reports informational, and a scored item with an empty set of conditions still fails. Items satisfiable either from a live process's argument list or from a settings file have those two sources crossed, so where the argument holds the wanted value and the file holds a different one the item now fails, and where the argument holds the unwanted value but the file agrees with expectations it now passes. An assertion that a parameter is simply absent, with no settings file in play, likewise reports the opposite of what the process listing shows. Every comparison of file permission bits is broken: a mode of 640, 444, 777 or 211 measured against an expected 644 no longer yields a verdict on whether it is at least as restrictiv
